newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY

- First in series of commentaries calling for further study of President Jiang Zemin's speech at a memorial meeting for late leader Deng Xiaoping on February 25. Commentary stresses need to be equipped with scientific theory
- Publication of full text of revised Criminal Law adopted at by National People's Congress on March 14.
- Tibet total trade worth $104 million in 1996, up 48.49 percent from the previous year
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- China to complete track-laying for 898.7-km electrified railway linking Nanning and Kunming
- Qiao Shi, chairman of National People's Congress, meets parliamentary delegation from Latvia led by Alfred Chepanis, chairman of Latvian parliament.
CHINA DAILY
- Official with Ministry of Public Security says regulations on entry and exit between interior areas and Hong Kong will remain unchanged after Hong Kong's return on July 1.
- Senior public servants from the Hong Kong British government to undergo four-week training course at Beijing's Qinghua University from April 2.
- Air quality of 10 major Chinese cities, including Beijing, Shanghai and Tianjin, to be monitored and made public every week from June 5
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Bank of Communications makes 5.37 billion yuan i profits in 1996
- Coal industry makes 1.55 billion yuan in profits in 1996, up 53.4 percent
- China seen to cut interest rates slightly in 1997
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China animal feed market seen improving as prices stabilise in 1997
- Hai'er Group tops electrical home appliance manufacturers in terms of sales in 1996
- China sells 12.3 billion yuan of record 123 billion yuan non-tradeable T-bond issue by March 7
BEIJING ECONOMIC DAILY
- Tianjin Automobile Co says not to cut car prices in 1997
- Beijing to use unleaded gasoline in inner city from July 1
